summary:
1. No zero-shot model here outputs rotation or corners. Open-vocabulary detectors return axis-aligned boxes only, so every useful pipeline must end in mask -> cv2.minAreaRect. Read colour from mask pixels (Lab/HSV), not from prompt words: attribute prompts are a documented weak point of Grounding-DINO/OWL-class detectors (OVDEval).
2. One package covers almost everything: transformers 5.24.1 with torch 2.15.0, torchvision 0.29.2, Python 3.12. It coexists with ultralytics 8.4.218 and rfdetr 1.12.1 (rfdetr itself requires transformers >=5.1,<6).
3. LEAN set, no login, 1,468 MB: facebook/sam2.1-hiera-tiny 156 MB + iSEE-Laboratory/llmdet_tiny 692 MB + google/owlv2-base-patch16-ensemble 620 MB. Smallest useful pair: SAM 2.1 tiny + LLMDet tiny = 848 MB. Small add-ons: EdgeTAM 56 MB, OmDet-Turbo 462 MB (needs timm).
4. Offer two combined "models": (a) text detector boxes -> SAM 2.1 box prompt -> minAreaRect + pixel colour; (b) SAM 2.1 segment-everything -> area/squareness filter -> minAreaRect + pixel colour (no text prompt).
5. HEAVY set, only after freeing about 8-10 GB: SAM 3 (text -> instance masks, the best conceptual fit) 3,440 MB, OWLv2-large 1,750 MB, LLMDet-large 1,376 MB, SAM 2.1 large 898 MB, Falcon-Perception 2,530 MB.
6. Login: only facebook/sam3 and facebook/sam3.1 are gated (gated=manual, HTTP 401 without a token, Meta must approve the request). Ungated third-party copies exist (unsloth/sam3.1 1,681 MB bf16; yonigozlan/sam3-litetext-s0 2,117 MB); the SAM License permits redistribution, but they are not Meta releases.
7. I found no published M-series latency for these models. Every latency and RAM figure below is an estimate unless a source is named; nothing was run. The lab should record wall time (after torch.mps.synchronize()) and peak memory per run.
8. Test first: wood cubes on white PLA (low contrast), and whether the area filter rejects the coloured basket floors.

candidates.what: Class-agnostic masks from point or box prompts, plus segment-everything through the transformers mask-generation pipeline. For the cubes it is the mask stage: each mask gives centre, angle mod 90 and 4 corners via cv2.minAreaRect. It has no notion of class, so colour comes from the pixels.
candidates.fit_for_task: Good fit as the mask stage and the cheapest model here (156 MB). A 61 px cube is large enough: SAM 2 resizes 1280x720 to 1024x1024, so a cube becomes about 49x87 px. The default 32x32 point grid puts at least one point on every cube (spacing 40x22 px); a 16x16 grid (80 px spacing) would miss cubes. Open risks, untested: wood on white PLA may not separate, and mask edges can include shadow, which biases the angle. Segment-everything also returns the board, baskets, basket floors and the arm, so an area/squareness filter is mandatory.
candidates.weights_id: facebook/sam2.1-hiera-tiny (model.safetensors; the repo also holds a duplicate sam2.1_hiera_tiny.pt, repo total 312 MB)
candidates.pip_package: transformers>=4.56.0 (Sam2Model first shipped in 4.56.0; target 5.24.1), torch, torchvision (the v5 image processor is torchvision-backed)
candidates.mps: works with CPU fallback. The official SAM 2 notebook sets PYTORCH_ENABLE_MPS_FALLBACK=1 and warns that MPS support is preliminary and may give numerically different or degraded output. No MPS-specific code in the transformers port; not run here.
candidates.latency_note: Estimate, not measured. Box/point prompt: well under 1 s per image on M4 MPS (one secondary blog reports about 1.6 s per single-point prompt on an M1). Segment-everything with 1024 points = 16 decoder batches plus full-resolution mask filtering and NMS: expect roughly 3-10 s per 1280x720 image. Official speed is 91.2 FPS on an A100 (video, compiled).
candidates.ram_note: Estimate: 1-2 GB process. Segment-everything upsamples 64 points x 3 masks to 720x1280 per batch (about 0.7 GB float32 transient); lower points_per_batch if memory is tight.
candidates.snippet:
import torch, numpy as np
from PIL import Image
from transformers import pipeline, Sam2Model, Sam2Processor

device = "mps" if torch.backends.mps.is_available() else "cpu"
mid = "facebook/sam2.1-hiera-tiny"
image = Image.open("frame.jpg").convert("RGB")

# (a) segment everything
gen = pipeline("mask-generation", model=mid, device=device)
out = gen(image, points_per_batch=64, points_per_crop=32,
          pred_iou_thresh=0.8, stability_score_thresh=0.9, output_bboxes_mask=True)
masks = [np.asarray(m, dtype=bool) for m in out["masks"]]   # HxW each; out["scores"], out["bounding_boxes"]

# (b) boxes -> masks
model = Sam2Model.from_pretrained(mid, dtype=torch.float32).to(device).eval()
proc = Sam2Processor.from_pretrained(mid)
boxes = [[[100, 100, 161, 161], [300, 220, 361, 281]]]      # [image][box][x1,y1,x2,y2] in pixels
inputs = proc(images=image, input_boxes=boxes, return_tensors="pt").to(device)
with torch.inference_mode():
    o = model(**inputs, multimask_output=False)
m = proc.post_process_masks(o.pred_masks.cpu(), inputs["original_sizes"])[0]   # (N,1,H,W) bool

candidates.fit_for_task: Small costs only 28 MB more than tiny and is a reasonable second choice. Large is unlikely to pay off for clean 61 px squares on a plain board; add it only if tiny/small masks leak into shadows or miss wood cubes.
candidates.mps: same as tiny (works with CPU fallback; preliminary per the official notebook)
candidates.latency_note: Estimate. Official A100 FPS: small 84.8, base-plus 64.1, large 39.5 against tiny 91.2. In segment-everything the decoder loop dominates, so the size mainly changes the one-off encoder pass.

candidates.family: Grounding DINO family (LLMDet, loaded through the MM-Grounding-DINO class)
candidates.what: Text-prompted box detector (Swin-T). Prompt such as ["a small cube", "a wooden block"] returns boxes with scores and text labels. For the cubes it proposes boxes that then go to SAM 2.1 as box prompts.
candidates.fit_for_task: Best single representative of the Grounding-DINO line: same 692 MB as Grounding DINO tiny, with clearly higher zero-shot LVIS numbers in the transformers docs (LLMDet-tiny 44.3 val AP vs MM-GDINO-tiny 31.9). Input is resized to 750x1333, so a cube is about 64 px: not a small-object problem. Limits: boxes are axis-aligned (no angle, no corners), and colour words in the prompt are unreliable, so prompt for the shape and classify colour from pixels. A cube seen from straight above is a flat square, so let the user edit prompts ("square block", "small box", "tile"). A prompt like "red square" will also hit the basket floors.
candidates.mps: unknown, expected to work. No MPS-specific code and no open MPS issue found; the deformable attention uses grid_sample, which MPS supports. Keep PYTORCH_ENABLE_MPS_FALLBACK=1 as a safety net.
candidates.latency_note: Estimate, not measured: about 0.5-1.5 s per 1280x720 image on M4 MPS, several seconds on CPU. No public M-series benchmark found.

candidates.what: Text-prompted detector with a different design from Grounding DINO: one box per image patch (3,600 candidates at 960x960), a class-agnostic objectness score, and image-guided detection, where a crop of one cube is the query instead of text.
candidates.fit_for_task: Worth including for two reasons the DINO family does not offer: objectness scores (find square things without naming them) and one-shot detection from an example cube crop, which avoids the wording problem. Weaker points: the 1280x720 frame is padded to a 1280x1280 square and resized to 960, so a cube is about 46 px, roughly 3 patches across; boxes are coarser than Grounding DINO's and many near-duplicates need NMS. Boxes only, no angle. Whether an exemplar crop separates R/G/B/wood is untested.

import torch
from PIL import Image
from transformers import Owlv2Processor, Owlv2ForObjectDetection

device = "mps" if torch.backends.mps.is_available() else "cpu"
mid = "google/owlv2-base-patch16-ensemble"
processor = Owlv2Processor.from_pretrained(mid)
model = Owlv2ForObjectDetection.from_pretrained(mid, dtype=torch.float32).to(device).eval()
image = Image.open("frame.jpg").convert("RGB")
sizes = torch.tensor([(image.height, image.width)])   # original size; padding is handled internally

# text prompts
text_labels = [["a photo of a small cube", "a photo of a wooden block"]]
inputs = processor(text=text_labels, images=image, return_tensors="pt").to(device)
with torch.inference_mode():
    outputs = model(**inputs)
res = processor.post_process_grounded_object_detection(
    outputs=outputs, target_sizes=sizes, threshold=0.1, text_labels=text_labels)[0]
# res["boxes"], res["scores"], res["text_labels"]; outputs.objectness_logits is class-agnostic

# one-shot: cube_crop is a PIL crop of one example cube
q = processor(images=image, query_images=cube_crop, return_tensors="pt").to(device)
with torch.inference_mode():
    qo = model.image_guided_detection(**q)
det = processor.post_process_image_guided_detection(
    outputs=qo, threshold=0.6, nms_threshold=0.3, target_sizes=sizes)[0]

candidates.snippet:
# boxes: (N,4) xyxy pixel tensor from the detector; sam / sam_proc = Sam2Model / Sam2Processor
import cv2, numpy as np, torch
inputs = sam_proc(images=image, input_boxes=[boxes.tolist()], return_tensors="pt").to(device)
with torch.inference_mode():
    o = sam(**inputs, multimask_output=False)
masks = sam_proc.post_process_masks(o.pred_masks.cpu(), inputs["original_sizes"])[0][:, 0].numpy()
lab = cv2.cvtColor(cv2.cvtColor(np.asarray(image), cv2.COLOR_RGB2BGR), cv2.COLOR_BGR2LAB)
cubes = []
for m in masks:
    m8 = m.astype(np.uint8)
    cnts, _ = cv2.findContours(m8, cv2.RETR_EXTERNAL, cv2.CHAIN_APPROX_SIMPLE)
    if not cnts:
        continue
    c = max(cnts, key=cv2.contourArea)
    area = cv2.contourArea(c)
    (cx, cy), (w, h), ang = cv2.minAreaRect(c)
    if not (2000 < area < 6500) or min(w, h) / max(w, h) < 0.8:   # 61x61 px cube is about 3700 px^2
        continue
    core = cv2.erode(m8, np.ones((7, 7), np.uint8)) > 0
    L, a, b = np.median(lab[core if core.any() else m], axis=0)   # map (L,a,b) to R/G/B/wood with tuned thresholds
    cubes.append({"center": (cx, cy), "angle": ang % 90,
                  "corners": cv2.boxPoints(((cx, cy), (w, h), ang)), "lab": (L, a, b)})

candidates.what: Text phrase (or exemplar box) in, instance masks + boxes + scores for every matching object out. For the cubes: prompt "cube" or "red cube" and get one mask per cube directly, then minAreaRect. 848M parameters, 1008x1008 input.
candidates.fit_for_task: Conceptually the best fit: one model returns per-instance masks for a noun phrase, and its README states the presence token improves discrimination between close prompts such as "a player in white" vs "a player in red". But it is the hardest to get onto this machine: gated with manual approval, 3.44 GB download with 5.7 GB free, and about 7 GB peak memory. Heavy set only. Whether "red cube" separates printed-paper colours and wood here is untested.
candidates.licence: SAM License (custom Meta licence; redistribution allowed under the same terms; excludes military, nuclear and weapons uses)
candidates.weights_id: facebook/sam3 (model.safetensors 3,439.9 MB; the repo also holds sam3.pt 3,450.1 MB, repo total 6,895 MB). facebook/sam3.1 is gated too and ships only sam3.1_multiplex.pt 3,502.8 MB (no transformers weights).

candidates.mps: works in transformers (unverified by run): MPS fixes were merged (PRs 43042, 43061). The official facebookresearch/sam3 code lists a CUDA GPU as a prerequisite and its MPS pull requests (400, 627) are still open.
candidates.latency_note: Derived estimate: about 1-4 s per image on M4 MPS, plus about 0.1-0.3 s per extra text prompt when vision features are reused. Basis: the sam3rs package reports 824 ms encode and 103 ms text prompt on an M4 Pro in bf16 and says that is 1.19x-2.9x faster than the official package on PyTorch MPS; PR 627 reports SAM 3.1 video at about 1.3 fps on an M5 16 GB.
candidates.ram_note: About 7 GB peak reported for SAM 3.1 on an M5 16 GB (PR 627, bf16). Float32 weights alone are 3.4 GB. Load it alone; unload other models first.
candidates.snippet:
import torch
from PIL import Image
from transformers import Sam3Model, Sam3Processor

device = "mps" if torch.backends.mps.is_available() else "cpu"
mid = "facebook/sam3"      # gated: approved access request + `hf auth login`
model = Sam3Model.from_pretrained(mid, dtype=torch.float32).to(device).eval()
processor = Sam3Processor.from_pretrained(mid)
image = Image.open("frame.jpg").convert("RGB")

img_in = processor(images=image, return_tensors="pt").to(device)
with torch.inference_mode():
    vision_embeds = model.get_vision_features(pixel_values=img_in.pixel_values)   # encode once
    for prompt in ["red cube", "green cube", "blue cube", "wooden cube"]:
        t = processor(text=prompt, return_tensors="pt").to(device)
        out = model(vision_embeds=vision_embeds, **t)
        r = processor.post_process_instance_segmentation(
            out, threshold=0.5, mask_threshold=0.5,
            target_sizes=img_in.get("original_sizes").tolist())[0]
        # r["masks"] (N,H,W) bool, r["boxes"] xyxy px, r["scores"]

It emits one token sequence at 768x768 input, so 9-12 near-identical small squares depend on the decoder enumerating every instance; there are no per-box confidence scores to threshold, and coordinates are quantised. Include only as a curiosity or if a caption/grounding view is wanted in the lab.
candidates.weights_id: florence-community/Florence-2-base (native transformers format, safetensors only). Large: florence-community/Florence-2-large 1,553.5 MB. The microsoft/Florence-2-* repos still carry auto_map remote code.
candidates.pip_package: transformers>=4.56.0 (Florence2ForConditionalGeneration is absent in 4.55.0, present in 4.56.0)
candidates.mps: unknown. Checkpoint dtype is float16 and transformers v5 loads in the checkpoint dtype by default, so pass dtype=torch.float32 on MPS/CPU.
candidates.latency_note: Estimate: 0.5-2 s per image on M4 MPS, growing with the number of generated boxes; num_beams=3 from the docs triples decoder work.
candidates.snippet:
import torch
from transformers import AutoProcessor, Florence2ForConditionalGeneration
mid = "florence-community/Florence-2-base"
model = Florence2ForConditionalGeneration.from_pretrained(mid, dtype=torch.float32).to(device).eval()
processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(mid)
task = "<OD>"   # text tasks append the phrase after the token, e.g. "<CAPTION_TO_PHRASE_GROUNDING>" + "small cubes" (convention from the model card, not re-checked on the native class)
inputs = processor(text=task, images=image, return_tensors="pt").to(device)
ids = model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=1024, num_beams=3)
text = processor.batch_decode(ids, skip_special_tokens=False)[0]
parsed = processor.post_process_generation(text, task=task, image_size=image.size)
# {'<OD>': {'bboxes': [[x1,y1,x2,y2], ...], 'labels': [...]}}

packaging: One environment is enough: Python 3.12, torch 2.15.0 (macOS arm64 wheel 138.6 MB), torchvision 0.29.2 (requires torch>=2.14.0), transformers 5.24.1 (requires Python>=3.11, huggingface-hub>=1.31.0,<3.0, tokenizers>=0.23.1,<0.24.0, safetensors>=0.8.0; its setup.py lists torch>=2.6). All versions are the latest on PyPI on 2026-11-25.

Minimum transformers release per class, checked by file presence at release tags: Owlv2ForObjectDetection 4.35.0; GroundingDinoForObjectDetection 4.40.0; OmDetTurboForObjectDetection 4.45.0; SamHQModel 4.52.1 (absent in 4.51.0; 4.52.0 not probed); MMGroundingDinoForObjectDetection (also loads LLMDet) 4.55.0; Sam2Model and Florence2ForConditionalGeneration 4.56.0; EdgeTamModel 4.57.0; Sam3Model 5.0.0 (absent in 4.57.6); Sam3LiteTextModel 5.6.0 (absent in 5.5.0).

No conflict with rfdetr or ultralytics: rfdetr 1.12.1 requires transformers>=5.1.0,<6.0.0, torch>=2.2.0, supervision>=0.29.0; ultralytics 8.4.218 has no transformers dependency. Because rfdetr forces transformers 5.x, use the native-format repos (florence-community/Florence-2-*) rather than older trust_remote_code repos.
ultralytics on macOS excludes numpy 2.0.* through 2.3.4; numpy 2.5.5 (requires Python>=3.12) satisfies it.

Extra packages: timm only for OmDet-Turbo (transformers lists timm>=1.0.23; latest 1.0.31). accelerate only if device_map=... is used (accelerate 1.16.0 requires torch>=2.6.0); the snippets use .to("mps") so it is not needed. opencv-python and numpy for the minAreaRect/colour step.

Do not install on this Mac: the official facebookresearch/sam3 package (README prerequisites list a CUDA GPU; pyproject pins numpy>=1.26,<2; open issues about triton and decord on macOS). groundingdino-py is likewise unnecessary because the transformers port covers it. The official sam2 1.1.0 package works (torch>=2.5.1, hydra-core, iopath) but adds nothing over Sam2Model.

Cache locations: HF_HOME defaults to ~/.cache/huggingface; HF_HUB_CACHE defaults to $HF_HOME/hub; HF_XET_CACHE defaults to $HF_HOME/xet; the token lives in $HF_HOME/token or the HF_TOKEN variable. TRANSFORMERS_CACHE was removed in transformers v5. Point HF_HOME at a folder inside the lab's data directory so model disk use is visible and removable in one place; set HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 after downloading to skip network checks.
Set PYTORCH_ENABLE_MPS_FALLBACK=1 before importing torch (the official SAM 2 notebook does this) so an unsupported MPS operator falls back to CPU instead of raising.

Disk: the sizes quoted are the single model.safetensors file. Many repos also hold duplicate .bin/.pt files (grounding-dino-tiny repo 1,382 MB, sam2.1-hiera-tiny repo 312 MB, facebook/sam3 repo 6,895 MB, unsloth/sam3.1 repo 4,777 MB), so never snapshot a whole repo without allow_patterns.

LEAN subset, no login: facebook/sam2.1-hiera-tiny 155.9 + iSEE-Laboratory/llmdet_tiny 692.0 + google/owlv2-base-patch16-ensemble 619.9 = 1,467.8 MB. Minimum pair (SAM 2.1 tiny + LLMDet tiny) = 847.9 MB. Optional small add-ons: yonigozlan/EdgeTAM-hf 55.9 MB, omlab/omdet-turbo-swin-tiny-hf 461.8 MB.

HEAVY subset, after freeing about 8-10 GB: facebook/sam3 3,439.9 (gated) or unsloth/sam3.1 1,680.9 or yonigozlan/sam3-litetext-s0 2,117.1; google/owlv2-large-patch14-ensemble 1,750.5; iSEE-Laboratory/llmdet_large 1,376.4; facebook/sam2.1-hiera-large 897.9; tiiuae/Falcon-Perception 2,529.5. With official SAM 3 the first four total 7,464.7 MB.

Login or licence click: only facebook/sam3 and facebook/sam3.1 (gated=manual; anonymous file request returns 401). They need a Hugging Face account, an access request that Meta approves, and `hf auth login` or HF_TOKEN. Every other repo listed is gated=false.
pitfalls: Axis-aligned boxes cannot give the rotation angle or the corners; a cube rotated 45 degrees has an 86 px box. Every detector must be followed by a mask step (SAM box prompt or classical contour) and cv2.minAreaRect.

Do not rely on colour words in prompts for the class. OVDEval (arXiv 2308.13177) reports that leading open-vocabulary detectors fail on attribute sub-tasks with hard negatives. Detect the shape, then classify colour from mask pixels.
Mission B basket floors are large R/G/B regions. Text prompts with colour words and segment-everything will both return them; filter by area (cube about 3,700 px^2) and squareness.

transformers v5 loads weights in the checkpoint dtype by default (dtype="auto"). Florence-2 community repos are float16 and unsloth/sam3.1 is bfloat16; pass dtype=torch.float32 explicitly on MPS/CPU unless half precision is known to work.
Docs examples use device_map="auto", which needs accelerate. Use .to("mps") instead.
The transformers EdgeTAM docs print the id yonigozlan/edgetam-1, which returns HTTP 401. The working public repo is yonigozlan/EdgeTAM-hf.
OmDet-Turbo fails to load without timm (use_timm_backbone=true in its config).
Segment-everything grid: the pipeline argument is points_per_crop (default 32, i.e. 1,024 points). On a 1280 px wide frame, fewer than about 21 points per side leaves gaps wider than a 61 px cube.
Mask-generation defaults (pred_iou_thresh 0.88, stability_score_thresh 0.95) are strict and can drop valid masks; expose them as run parameters.

OWLv2 pads the frame to a square before resizing. Current post-processing already scales boxes by max(height, width), so pass the original (height, width) and do not correct again. It returns many overlapping boxes; apply class-agnostic NMS.

SAM 2 and SAM 3 resize to a fixed square (1024 and 1008) without keeping aspect ratio; masks come back at original size, so no manual correction is needed. Lowering SAM 3 resolution is documented to degrade accuracy.
MPS timing: call torch.mps.synchronize() before stopping the clock and discard the first run.
16 GB unified memory: keep one heavy model loaded at a time; before switching, delete the model, run gc.collect() and torch.mps.empty_cache(). SAM 3 needs about 7 GB peak by itself.
Video: all of these are 1 fps-class or slower on this machine. Offer a frame stride or a frame range rather than per-frame inference on whole clips.
facebook/sam3 access is approved manually; it may not arrive before 2026-11-29.

Ungated SAM 3 copies (unsloth/sam3.1, jetjodh/sam3, 1038lab/sam3, yonigozlan/sam3-litetext-s0) are third-party redistributions. The SAM License permits redistribution under the same agreement, but they are not Meta releases; the SAM3-LiteText card labels itself Apache-2.0, which is unclear for SAM 3-derived weights.
Licences that restrict use: EdgeSAM is non-commercial (S-Lab License 1.0); WeDetect is GPL-3.0.
The sam3rs runtime (fast SAM 3 on Metal) requires macOS 26.1 or newer, so it does not run on macOS 15.7.
open_questions: Nothing was executed. Do LLMDet-tiny, OWLv2-base and SAM 2.1 tiny actually run on MPS with torch 2.15.0 without CPU fallback, and what are the real latency and peak memory on the M4 16 GB?
Are plain wood cubes on white PLA detected and segmented at all (low contrast)? This decides whether any zero-shot route is viable for the wood class.
Which prompt wording finds top-down cubes best: "cube", "block", "square", "small box", "tile"?
Does OWLv2 image-guided detection with one cube crop find all cubes, and does it separate colours or return all cubes regardless of colour?
Does SAM 3 / 3.1 separate "red cube", "green cube", "blue cube" and "wooden cube" on printed paper colours under the venue lighting?
Does bfloat16 inference work on MPS for unsloth/sam3.1, or must it be loaded as float32 (3.4 GB)?
Is using an ungated third-party SAM 3 copy acceptable to the user, or should the lab wait for the official gated access?
How much disk can be freed? With 5.7 GB free, the Python environment plus the lean set plus uploaded videos and results leaves little margin; the heavy set is out until that changes.
Do SAM masks include the cube's shadow or side faces enough to bias minAreaRect angle and centre? Needs a check against a hand-measured frame.
How many faces carry coloured paper? If the top face can be plain wood on a coloured cube, pixel-colour classification from the top view cannot recover the class.
